New York · Wed Nov 18 – Sun Nov 22, 2026

Four nights of Manhattan after dark

Late mornings, one good thing each afternoon, your three fixed evenings, and a hidden bar after each one. Everything starts and ends at Deb's place on 9th Avenue, so most of it is a short walk or a ten-minute cab. Every stop has a Plan B underneath it, something close by to swap in if it's booked or you change your mind.

Wednesday, Nov 18

Arrival night
10:29p

Land at JFK, cab straight to Deb's

Take the yellow-cab line, not a hailing driver inside the terminal. JFK to Manhattan is a flat fare plus tolls and surcharges, so expect roughly $90–110 with tip. At that hour it's 40–50 minutes to 9th Ave & 38th.

Thursday, Nov 19

You + Deb's friend by day · group for the show
11:45a

Lunch at Keens, 1885

The ceilings hold tens of thousands of old clay churchwarden pipes from the members' pipe club; Teddy Roosevelt and Babe Ruth had theirs here. This is the dark-wood, leather-banquette New York you're after, in daylight. Go light in the Pub Room with the burger or the mutton chop to share, since Saturday is a steak night.

72 W 36th St · 15-min walkOpens 11:45am weekdays
Book on OpenTable212-947-3636
Plan B if Keens is booked
  • Gallaghers, 228 W 52nd. A 1927 steakhouse with the dry-aging meat locker in the front window and photos of old boxers and jockeys on the walls. The three-course lunch is about $34, served from 11:45. A 10-minute cab, and it puts you closer to the Intrepid. Book
1:30p

Intrepid Museum and the Space Shuttle Enterprise

The ship you were thinking of is the Intrepid, an aircraft carrier turned museum at Pier 86; the shuttle on board is the Enterprise, NASA's first orbiter, in its own pavilion on the flight deck. Give it about two and a half hours: the shuttle pavilion, the jets on deck, the hangar deck exhibits.

Pier 86, W 46th St & 12th Ave · 10-min cab10am–5pm · adults about $32 online

A third-party guide lists the Exploreum and flight simulators closing from 3pm that day. Not on the official site, so check when you buy; it doesn't affect the shuttle.

Buy timed tickets
Plan B / swap nearby
  • MoMA: Brancusi, The Artist and His Studio. The first big Brancusi retrospective in 30 years, about 210 sculptures, tools and photos from his Paris studio (through Feb 27). Book a timed ticket; the galleries get crowded. 11 W 53rd, 10-min cab. MoMA
  • Circle Line from Pier 83, next door to the Intrepid. The Landmarks cruise runs down the Hudson to the Statue of Liberty and back in about 90 minutes. Check sailing times for the day. Circle Line
4:15p

Winter Village at Bryant Park, as the lights come on

Sunset is 4:35, so you get the market glowing. It's about 180 holiday kiosks around a rink, a block from the theater. Eat here instead of a sit-down dinner: walk the stalls, grab a hot drink and something hot to eat at the kiosks, then stroll to the show. Save skating for Rockefeller on Saturday.

42nd St between 5th & 6th · 15-min cab from the pierFree to walk
Winter Village info
Plan B / swap nearby
  • A pre-show drink at The Rum House, 228 W 47th. A candlelit, wood-paneled bar off the Hotel Edison lobby with a pianist or jazz most nights. Walk-in, 5 minutes from the theater, and the closest thing to old Times Square that's left.
  • Union Square Holiday Market. The other big holiday market, open since about Nov 12; 15 minutes by subway. More crafts, fewer tourists than Bryant Park.
7:00p

Michelle Wolf: Best Job in the World

The Town Hall is a 1921 hall with famously good acoustics, which helps stand-up more than you'd think. Doors usually open 30 minutes before; arrive by 6:40 to get settled.

BookedThe Town Hall · 123 W 43rd St7:00–9:00pm
Event page
9:15p

Bar Centrale, up the unmarked stairs

A 12-minute walk west along 46th Street. There's no sign: an unmarked door between Joe Allen and Orso, then a flight of stairs to a small, dim room where Broadway actors drink after their shows. Book by phone; the bar closes at 11:30pm.

324 W 46th StPhone only · (212) 581-3130Business casual
Plan B if Plan A is booked
  • Plan B: The Campbell, inside Grand Central, a 10-minute walk east. Book on Resy (9:30 and 10pm were open on Nov 14).
  • Plan C: The Rum House, 228 W 47th, 5 minutes from the theater. Walk-in, candlelit, live piano or jazz, open late.
  • Plan D: Madame George, 45 W 45th, a plush live-music den 4 minutes away.

Friday, Nov 20

You + Deb's friend by day · Friendsgiving at 6
10:00a

Walk the Brooklyn Bridge, Brooklyn back to Manhattan

Walk it toward Manhattan, so the skyline is in front of you the whole way instead of behind you. Take the A or C from 34th St–Penn Station to High St in Brooklyn (about 20 minutes; leave Deb's at 10). Start with ten minutes in DUMBO: Washington St at Water St is the famous shot of the Manhattan Bridge framed between old warehouses. Then walk the 1.1 miles across on the raised wooden walkway, about 40 minutes with photo stops, and come off at City Hall.

Start: High St station (A/C) · End: Brooklyn Bridge–City HallFree · no booking

Weekday mornings are the quietest time on the bridge. From City Hall, the 4 or 5 express gets you to Grand Central in about 10 minutes, so you're there by noon with time to look around the main concourse before lunch.

Plan B if it's raining
  • The Morgan Library, 225 Madison at 36th. J.P. Morgan's private library from 1906: three tiers of walnut bookcases, a painted ceiling, Gutenberg Bibles under glass. Quiet and grand at its 10:30 opening; an hour is enough, then it's a 10-minute walk to Grand Central. About $25, timed tickets suggested. Tickets
  • Or move the bridge to Sunday morning. Leave Deb's at 9, walk it, and you're back by noon for the 12:45 airport cab. Brunch becomes a coffee and something to go in DUMBO.
12:30p

Grand Central: Oyster Bar, then the Whispering Gallery

Lunch under the tiled vaults of the Oyster Bar, open since 1913; the pan roast is the classic order. On the way out, stand in opposite corners of the tiled arch outside its entrance and whisper into the wall. The other person hears you clearly 30 feet away.

Lower level, Grand Central · 10 min from City Hall on the 4/5Weekdays from 11:30am · closed weekends
Book on OpenTable212-490-6650
Plan B / swap nearby
  • No table: Urbanspace Vanderbilt, the food hall across the street at 45th & Vanderbilt. Quick, good, and you keep the Whispering Gallery, which is free and needs no booking.
  • Something else to see: the Chrysler Building lobby, a 3-minute walk east at Lexington & 42nd. The Art Deco lobby is all red marble, chrome and a painted ceiling, free on weekdays. The building recently changed hands and is up for renovation, so check the door is open.
2:15p

Rose Main Reading Room, New York Public Library

Two blocks over. Two football fields of oak tables under a painted sky ceiling. Fifteen minutes is enough, and it's free.

5th Ave at 42ndFree
Hours
Plan B / swap nearby
  • The Morgan Library (if the bridge kept you outdoors). A 10-minute walk down Madison; it's the same wow, dark wood instead of oak, with more to see.
  • The Chrysler Building lobby, if you skipped it at lunch.
  • Or just sit in Bryant Park behind the library with a hot drink before SUMMIT; the Winter Village is right there.
3:30p

SUMMIT One Vanderbilt, timed for sunset

This is the observation deck that isn't a line: you book a timed slot, then walk through mirrored rooms that make the skyline repeat to infinity, glass ledges hanging off the 91st floor, and a room of drifting silver balloons. The Empire State Building is right in your view. Book the 3:30 slot to catch the 4:35 sunset; sunset slots cost about $10–13 extra and sell out first.

45 E 42nd St, next to Grand CentralAbout $45–60 per person · 75–90 min inside

Wear pants or shorts rather than a skirt (mirrored floors), and sunglasses help in the mirror rooms at sunset.

Book sunset slot
Plan B if sunset is sold out
  • Top of the Rock, 30 Rockefeller Plaza. Also timed tickets, open-air, and the view has the Empire State Building in front and Central Park behind. A 10-minute walk from Grand Central. Tickets
  • Edge at Hudson Yards, 10 minutes from Deb's: the glass-floored outdoor deck, plus an indoor kaleidoscope room that opened in June. Good if you'd rather end the afternoon on the west side. Tickets
5:00p

One drink at The Campbell

Inside Grand Central, up a staircase most commuters never notice: the 1920s office of financier John W. Campbell, with a 25-foot hand-painted ceiling, a huge leaded window and a stone fireplace. Old-school luxe at its best, and a perfect pre-dinner stop before cabbing to Deb's.

15 Vanderbilt Ave (at 43rd), inside Grand CentralReservations recommended
The Campbell
Plan B if The Campbell is booked
  • Patent Pending, 49 W 27th. A real hidden bar: you walk through a coffee shop to a door in the back. Walk-in seats from 5pm, so no booking is needed at this hour. A 10-minute cab, then 15 minutes to Deb's.
6:00p

Friendsgiving at Deb's

Cab over at 5:40 (about 15 minutes crosstown at that hour). Drinks and catered Thanksgiving bites, then the group heads out. Deb's invite says as much.

BookedDeb's place
10:15p

Raines Law Room at The William

An 8–10 minute cab east. Parlor rooms tucked inside a Murray Hill hotel: velvet curtains, tufted armchairs, wallpaper and a fireplace, with cocktails made with care. Tables were wide open on Resy for Friday as of Nov 14.

24 E 39th St (Madison/Park)Resy · up to 8 people
Plan B if Plan A is booked
  • Plan B: Patent Pending, 49 W 27th, through a coffee shop to a door in the back. Walk-ins welcome from 5pm (reservations optional). 10-min cab.
  • Plan C: The Flatiron Room NoMad, 37 W 26th. Leather, dark wood, a wall of 1,000 whiskies and live jazz most nights. Book: 212-725-3866.
  • Plan D: Dear Irving, 55 Irving Pl in Gramercy. Velvet parlor rooms, each a different era. 12-min cab.

Saturday, Nov 21

You + Deb's friend + Deb, all day
11:00a

Walk the High Line south

The north end starts at Hudson Yards, about ten minutes from Deb's. Walk the elevated park south for about 30 minutes, through the Chelsea galleries and between the buildings, and drop down at 16th Street.

Enter at W 34th St & 12th Ave or Hudson YardsFree · opens 7am
High Line map
Plan B / swap nearby
  • The Met: Krasner and Pollock, Past Continuous. If it's cold or wet, spend the morning here instead: the Met's first major show on either painter, tracing the married couple's careers side by side (through Jan 31). A 15-minute cab; meet back up downtown after. The Met
11:45a

Brunch at Chelsea Market

An old Nabisco factory turned food hall, so everyone picks their own: Los Tacos No. 1 is the line worth joining. Lobster rolls, Italian and coffee are all inside too.

75 9th Ave at 16thWalk-in
Vendor list
Plan B if it's packed
  • Pastis, 52 Gansevoort. A sit-down French brasserie brunch 3 minutes away in the Meatpacking District, with zinc bar, white tiles and steak frites. Book ahead for Saturday. Pastis
12:45p

Little Island

A park on 132 concrete tulips over the Hudson, opened in 2021, so it's new since many people's last visit. Climb the paths to the overlooks, then walk back across the bridge. Free, and no timed entry needed on a November afternoon.

Pier 55 at W 13th St · 10-min walkFree
Little Island
Plan B / swap nearby
  • The Whitney: artport, A History of Internet Art. It opens to the public this very day, Sat Nov 21, on the 6th floor: 25 years of web art, from early browser pieces to AI work. The Whitney sits at the High Line's south end, 5 minutes from Little Island, and its outdoor terraces have great Hudson views. Whitney
2:30p

Skate at The Rink at Rockefeller Center

No standing in line: book a timed General Skate slot (from about $22) or the new VIP Skate, which opened Nov 14 with the new Skate House. The tree usually arrives mid-November and stays dark until the lighting in early December, so expect scaffolding around it. Cab from Little Island takes about 20 minutes.

Rockefeller Plaza, 49th–50th StBook for 3 · 2:30pm slot
Reserve skate time
Plan B if 2:30 is sold out
  • Wollman Rink, Central Park. Arguably the better skate: a bigger rink with the skyline over the trees, open since Oct 28 with tickets online. It's at 59th St inside the park, a few minutes' walk from the carriage line, so skating, carriage and dinner become one walk. Book a 3:00 slot and do the carriage at 4:30. Wollman tickets
  • The Rockettes instead of skating. The Christmas Spectacular is on at Radio City, across the street from the rink, through Jan 4: 90 minutes, no intermission, with a new number this year. Check for a Saturday matinee. Tickets
4:10p

Horse-carriage ride through Central Park at sunset

Good news: the carriages are still running. The City Council voted in late October to end them, but the ban wouldn't take effect until June 2028 (and as of late October it still needed the mayor's signature). Walk up Fifth Avenue past St. Patrick's (about 15 minutes) to the carriage line on Central Park South. No booking: pick a driver, agree the route and the posted city fare before you get in, and ride into the 4:35 sunset.

Central Park South, 5th–6th AvesAbout 20–45 min · bring a scarf

This part of Central Park South is a block from Bourbon Steak, so you'll know the walk for tonight.

Plan B if you'd rather skip it
  • Walk it instead: in at 59th & 6th, up The Mall under the elms to Bethesda Terrace and the fountain, then back. About 40 minutes, free, the same scenery at a slower pace.
5:00p

Back to Deb's to change

A 15-minute cab. Two hours to rest and dress for dinner: jacket, no sneakers.

7:30p

Bourbon Steak New York

Michael Mina's steakhouse inside the 1931 Essex House, facing the park, so the carriage ride and dinner sit on the same block. Leave Deb's at 7:10. The bar and lounge stay open until 1am if dinner runs long.

Polly's, downstairs on 55th

A 5-minute walk from Bourbon Steak. A red-curtained 1920s room hidden below Tanner Smith's, with cocktails around $18. Resy opens only 48 hours ahead, so book it Thursday.

12:45p

Leave for JFK, earlier than feels necessary

This is the Sunday before Thanksgiving week, one of the busiest travel days of the year. Leave Deb's by 12:45 for the 3:45 flight from Terminal 5.

On this week only

Exhibits and events running Nov 18–22, if you want to change things last minute
Opens Sat Nov 21 · Whitney

artport: A History of Internet Art

Opening day falls on your Saturday. 25 years of art made for the web, plus the world premiere of a live performance piece, Human Unreadable Act III, in the museum's theater on Nov 19, 21 and 22 (separate ticket).

Fits: Saturday, at the bottom of the High Line.

whitney.org
Through Jan 31 · The Met

Krasner and Pollock: Past Continuous

The Met's first major show on either painter, and the first big New York show on either in over 20 years. The husband and wife are hung side by side, so you see who influenced whom.

Fits: a rainy morning, any day.

metmuseum.org
Through Feb 27 · MoMA

Brancusi: The Artist and His Studio

About 210 objects from his Paris studio: the polished bronzes, the Endless Column pieces, his tools and his own photographs. Possible only because the Paris studio is closed for renovation.

Fits: Thursday instead of the Intrepid. Go early; it's crowded.

moma.org
Through Jan 4 · Radio City

Christmas Spectacular with the Rockettes

The longest run the show has ever had, with a new number this year. 90 minutes, no intermission, across the street from the Rockefeller rink.

Fits: Saturday afternoon, instead of skating.

rockettes.com
Now open · Bryant Park & Union Sq

Holiday markets

Bryant Park's Winter Village is already in the plan for Thursday. The Union Square market (open since about Nov 12) is the craftier, less touristy one. Columbus Circle's doesn't open until Dec 1.

Fits: any afternoon gap.

Urbanspace markets
Evenings · Chelsea Market

ARTECHOUSE: SUBMERGE

A digital-art room in Chelsea Market's old boiler room, with floor-to-ceiling projected worlds. Hour-long sessions, evenings only (Friday about 6–8pm, Saturday 6–10pm); confirm the run before you go.

Fits: an alternative if the Friendsgiving crowd wants an outing.

artechouse.com

Just missing it: Saks Fifth Avenue unveils its windows and light show on Monday Nov 23, the day after you fly home, and the Rockefeller tree is lit in early December. You'll see the tree going up, still under wraps.
